discovery: Programmable quantum matter with Rydberg-interacting neutral-atom arrays

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller, with coworkers, proposed the Rydberg blockade as a mechanism for fast, controllable entanglement between neutral atoms, and laid the theoretical foundations for quantum simulation with cold atoms. Browaeys and Lukin turned this idea into a new experimental platform: individually trapped atoms in reconfigurable optical tweezer arrays, coupled through Rydberg interactions. Browaeys demonstrated the blockade between two atoms and built defect-free arrays for quantum magnetism; Lukin's team realised hundreds of programmable qubits, observed quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquid signatures, and achieved high-fidelity parallel gates and logical qubits with error correction. This platform has transformed how we create, control and measure entangled many-body states, and its techniques now feed back into metrology, including tweezer-array optical clocks and entanglement-enhanced sensing. It is a decades-long programme where precise theory and exquisite experimental control together opened a new domain of physics.
